chapters.artifact: A remarkably preserved jar in a buried chamber
chapters.sourceSummary: An excavation fractures around the Archaeologist. Itoku rises through smoke, calls three players first, then four more through lightning. The narrator escapes but finds no public trace of the event.

chapters.mappingNote: Direct faction match; retain source ruler identity separately from the current faction's cultural label.
chapters.sourceSummary: Touching a jade disk turns an archaeological cave into an ancient gathering. Yu explains that he must compete before he can rest, and his players depart through the haze.

chapters.mappingNote: Direct match to the expanded game's Mali faction.
chapters.setting: Timbuktu manuscripts and the Sankarani river
chapters.artifact: A manuscript marked with football symbols, followed by an inscribed football
chapters.sourceSummary: The Archaeologist deciphers a manuscript and glimpses players around the city. The ruler remains unseen. A marked football in the river confirms the discovery and the next destination arrives as a message.

chapters.setting: Delhi and Patna, ending beside the Ganges
chapters.artifact: An engraved football drawn from river mud
chapters.sourceSummary: Messages and symbolic clues draw the narrator toward the Ganges. A marked football precedes the appearance of the ruler's players on a passing boat. Another symbolic sign points to Mexico.

chapters.mappingNote: The current game has Mayans and Aztecs, but neither is interchangeable with the book's Mixtec faction. Preserve a distinct future identity.
chapters.artifact: An obsidian blade and a football used in a summoning ritual
chapters.sourceSummary: The narrator deliberately performs a ritual. Lord Four Deer appears, names Itoku as a rival and reveals his players within the fire before disappearing.

chapters.mappingNote: An Arverni-specific expedition within the game's broader Gaul faction; do not relabel all Gaul history as Arverni.
chapters.artifact: Four resting rulers and a falcon omen
chapters.sourceSummary: The entire episode shifts into playful rhyme. Celtillus emerges, his players are named with comic appraisal, and a falcon's pose supplies the next clue toward Egypt.

chapters.setting: Abydos, near a small excavated shrine
chapters.artifact: A black granite stela with mixed scripts and a football symbol
chapters.sourceSummary: The narrator finds a new-looking inscription in an ancient place. A divine proclamation names Narmer's players as instruments of conquest; the Archaeologist answers its confidence with a dry aside.

chapters.artifact: Earlier expedition relics joined by ivory and a coin
chapters.sourceSummary: Relics from earlier chapters become part of a new offering. Malchus appears quietly by the sea while his players ride past. When the Archaeologist questions the roster's many tight ends, the ruler is already gone.

chapters.mappingNote: Norwegian ruler tradition within the game's broader Vikings faction.
chapters.artifact: A weathered runestone illuminated by moonlight
chapters.sourceSummary: The Archaeologist waits in the cold until the runestone shines blue. Its saga names the players and describes Haakon's arrival in the divine realm.

chapters.mappingNote: Kish-specific identity within broader Mesopotamia; preserve the source's chosen setting rather than treating it as verified geography.
chapters.sourceSummary: The narrator seeks a written message among the ruins. Clay cylinders bear Jushur's declaration and describe the players through an epic account of shared trials.

chapters.mappingNote: A Hunnic episode within the game's broader Warhorsemen faction; not an equivalence with every steppe culture.
chapters.setting: A long search ending among old walls in Istanbul
chapters.artifact: A wall poem and a burned black handprint
chapters.sourceSummary: The ruler remains elusive in the steppe. A message finally appears far away, followed by horns and a falcon's cry; the narrator senses an approaching army that nobody else perceives.

chapters.mappingNote: Kushite episode within the game's broader Nubia faction.
chapters.setting: Napata and a chamber near El-Kurru
chapters.artifact: A granite stela found by following a hawk
chapters.sourceSummary: A circling hawk guides the narrator into a narrow chamber. An inscription names Alara and his players, echoing the Egyptian discovery while retaining its own location and guide.

chapters.setting: Santa Sabina transforming into a battlefield vision
chapters.artifact: A sacred interior that opens onto an army's past
chapters.sourceSummary: The Archaeologist becomes an unseen observer of a Roman army. Ancus names the players through a rousing and increasingly absurd speech, then the charge returns the narrator to the present.

chapters.mappingNote: The chapter uses Macedon while describing Actaeus of Attica. Retain this source discrepancy; do not present it as verified historical lineage.
chapters.setting: A cave on an unnamed Aegean island
chapters.artifact: A bronze shield bearing the ruler's name
chapters.sourceSummary: A threatening apparition becomes a generous host. The cave transforms into a feast, the narrator jokes about the lineup, and the scene abruptly vanishes.

chapters.mappingNote: No direct Dål Riata faction exists. Do not silently substitute Inis Fáil; preserve this as a distinct source identity and special-event reference.
chapters.setting: A golf bunker at St. Andrews opening into Osiris's sanctum
chapters.artifact: A hidden passage beneath ordinary sand
chapters.sourceSummary: The narrator's vacation becomes a final summons. Osiris gathers the fourteen rulers, explains the contest, and Fergus violently replaces Sundiata before revealing his own players. The narrator returns to the same golf shot.

originalHistory.label: The original league · 2021–2023
originalHistory.description: Recorded results from the founder’s original Duat league. These are a historical exhibit and do not award wins or honors to this campaign.
notes: Source spellings and original faction labels are retained except the obvious heading typo Emporer is displayed as Emperor. Original record tables may reflect older rules and are not recomputed under this game’s scoring.
